newsitem.title: USA: RJR Nabisco sees strong Q4, promising 1997.
newsitem.headline: RJR Nabisco sees strong Q4, promising 1997.

text.p: RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp is looking forward to a very strong fourth quarter and believes the trends continue to be most promising for next year, chief executive Steven F. Goldstone said Monday.
The company reported fully diluted third quarter earnings per share of $0.68, before a $0.02 restructuring charge. That's up 11 percent from $0.61 a year earlier, RJR noted.
Net sales were up 7 percent to $4.35 billion, it added.
The First Call third quarter consensus estimate was $0.67 per share.

"Our latest quarterly results were ahead of expectations, representing strong performances from all three of our major business units and placing RJR Nabisco in the top-tier of consumer products for the period," Goldstone said.
"Sales and profits were up in domestic tobacco, international tobacco regained volume momentum and Nabisco's core domestic cookie and cracker business showed renewed strength."
"We are looking forward to a very strong fourth quarter and will enter 1997 with considerable momentum. We believe the trends continue to be most promising for next year," he said.
